body.p: Earlier, there was always a shaman here. Two Evenks died. He dreamt, he found [= saw that] they were killed [DCh]: Second part of the clause is not clear.close by. In the dream he started to see a shaman, who lived on a mountain. That one had eaten the Evenki. The shaman saw this in a dream, so he went to the mountaineer. He took fifty Evenki with him. He left, crossed [GVY:] há»¥rrÃ¤n 'the Yenisei and went along the river mouth of [the river] Pit. He met the others. There was a shaman on the other side [of the river].dives' is probably misprinted hururÃ¤n 'went' They met by the river mouth of Pit and talked. They talked and talked and the shaman asked the other one: "Where are you going?" "I walk along this [path]." They walked together along the river Pit and fifty Evenki became a hundred. They walked away from the river mouth for five days. They arrived. The two shamans walked along two traces. One walked across the land for three days. On the third day the shaman said: "We will walk one day then we will see the smoke coming from the big mountain." On [the mountain] Namur there are houses, forty houses. They walked quickly, walked around, the shamans' Evenki surrounded [them]. The shaman said: "Light fires." He forced his Evenkis, leading them around it. The Evenki started to shout, preparing to go to war. Again they started to shout, they shouted three times. The mountaineers did not come out. An old man warned them, having untied his string [=shoelaces?]. That shaman said: "Leave now and prepare to fight." The old man went back. They shouted, were still shouting, the old man came, again the shaman scolded that one, again he went home. The mountaineers' shamans came, moving their coats (?). They came, prepared their swords, the two shamans sat down together. The shaman who had eaten the Evenki said: "Why, we do not know anything about the ones that were eaten." He asked to marry three women. The other said: "I will give [them to you]." The local stopped ranting now. The Namur shamans said: "Now, be our visitors." They became guests, they visited for a long time, for seven days. He said while leaving that they were not to do it like that, they were not to repeat it, they were not to catch them again. The local shaman said: "Do not do it like that, now they will not leave the dogs there." The shaman gave the mountaineer three women. They left for the houses with the stinking women. They carried them across the water. They made the ogre go away, they left, they fought, half of them came apart, a few came with tied hands and wounds. Half of them were not there. The other ones left for home, they were not visible. They came home, they brought two beautiful women.
